limitations: Software-lab qualification only; no physical NIC/device or uncoached human-pilot qualification.
Windows application checks use independent loopback peers; Windows Npcap physical-driver fault behavior is unqualified.
Linux arm64 is cross-built and has no runtime qualification in this profile.
MQTT enhanced authentication, unsupported DNP3 authentication/object/link-control forms, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 remain unsupported.
Fault observations and compared responses do not establish an industrial-device crash or other field fault without target-side evidence.

The five two-hour matrices run on GitHub-hosted native Windows/Linux workers; Linux packet peers use owned namespaces and virtual Ethernet. Hosted provenance and independent validation proofs are retained.
The tls-handshake case observes fresh verified TLS handshakes only. Captured application replay remains incomplete and no application response match is claimed without usable TLS secrets.
TLS client-certificate authentication and HTTP/2/3 application replay are outside the supported CLI scope.
Two-hour matrices cover the built-in cases; custom rule packs, IPv6 TCP/UDP and captured TLS 1.3 combinations have regression coverage, not additional two-hour matrix qualification.

IEC 60870-5-104 replay, plain and inside TLS, and multi-session TLS replay are covered by regression tests, a controlled loopback outstation and operator replay of a field capture, not by an additional two-hour matrix case.
